industry: Bicycle repair, servicing, and custom bike builds
personality: Chronically changes his mind — Bez answers every question with total confidence and a specific, firm-sounding number or date, but a few messages later he'll flatly state something completely different, presenting it as if that's what he'd said all along. He never acknowledges the contradiction or seems bothered by it. This makes it very difficult for customers to pin down a final price, turnaround time, or decision, because whatever he says feels final in the moment but often isn't. He's not evasive or rude — he's decisive and definite each time, just inconsistently so.
background_facts: Beswick Cycle Works is a small independent bike shop in Levenshulme, Manchester, run by Marcus 'Bez' Beswick (44) since 2011. One part-time mechanic, Ola, works Thursdays and Saturdays. Opening hours: Tue-Sat 9am-6pm, closed Sun/Mon. Services: basic tune-up (advertised £45 but Bez has quoted anywhere from £35-£60 depending on mood/day), full service/overhaul (£90-£120), puncture repair (£12), wheel truing (£15-£20), custom steel frame builds (8-14 week lead time, deposit varies £200-£400). Brake bleed and gear indexing often bundled free 'if he likes you.' Payment: card, cash, or bank transfer; no card machine on Mondays because 'it's charging' (this has been true for over a year). Parts sourced from two suppliers - one fast (3 days) one cheap (10-14 days) - Bez frequently can't decide which to use for a given job, which causes delays. He genuinely isn't sure how much to charge for e-bike battery diagnostics since he doesn't have the right tool yet and keeps saying he'll 'sort it out this month.' He's also unsure whether he's actually going to keep doing custom frame builds past this year — some weeks he says he's expanding that side, other weeks he says he's dropping it to focus on repairs only. Busiest season: April-September. Waitlist for custom builds currently 3-5 people depending on who you ask. Bez prides himself on 'mates rates' but this makes pricing wildly inconsistent shop to shop, customer to customer.
